text:
# 什么是结构化答案区块？

- 原标题：What Is Structured Answer Block?
- 作者：Flavio Amiel Roborank 创始人
- 原文更新日期：2026-07-15
- 原文：https://roborank.io/glossary/structured-answer-block/
- 栏目：[AI Search & GEO](https://roborank.io/ai-search/)
- 说明：中文全文翻译，后附英文原文。原文中的数据、观点、平台说明及推广内容均按原文保留，未经独立验证。

---

## 中文全文

结构化答案区块，是一段自成一体的文字，常见形式是一个问题配一个简短答案、一个定义或一段直接概述，其写法使搜索或 AI 系统能够将其整体提取，作为对查询的回答。它直白陈述一个观点，不需要页面其他内容提供上下文，有时还会用 FAQPage 结构化数据等标记加以强化。

### 核心要点

- 结构化答案区块将清楚的问题或查询，与自成一体的答案配对，让引擎无需页面其余部分就能提取使用。
- FAQPage 结构化数据是与答案区块联系最密切的 [schema.org](http://schema.org) 标记，但即使完全没有标记，答案区块也能赢得 AI 引用和精选摘要。
- 2023 年 8 月，Google 宣布 FAQ 富媒体搜索结果仅对权威政府和医疗健康网站展示；此后又彻底停止在搜索中展示 FAQ 富媒体结果，相关调整从 2026 年 5 月 7 日开始推出。
- 答案区块持久的价值在于可提取性：能够被单独引用而仍然成立的段落，才是 AI 答案、精选摘要和“其他人还问”会选择的内容。

### 结构化答案区块如何运作

检索或答案引擎引用的不是页面，而是段落。Google 生成精选摘要，或 AI 系统撰写 [AI 概览](https://roborank.io/glossary/ai-overviews/)时，会扫描候选文档，寻找能够独立回答查询、几乎不需要修改就能展示的一段文字。结构化答案区块，就是刻意设计成这种形态的内容：一个明确或隐含的问题，后面紧接简短、自成一体的回答。

让区块成为“结构化”的关键，与其说是标记，不如说是表达形式。答案放在最前面，而不是把重点埋在铺垫之下；它也不会留下悬空的指代，让读者必须回看页面其他部分。这就是[答案优先写作](https://roborank.io/glossary/answer-first-writing/)的要求：第一句先表达观点，再提供支持。这样写成的区块具有[可提取性](https://roborank.io/glossary/extractability/)，也就是在完全没有周边上下文时，被复制进答案仍然讲得通。以“如上所述，这取决于几个因素”开头的区块，无论内容多么正确，都无法被直接提取。

标记可以为机器标注这个区块。例如，FAQPage 结构化数据告诉解析器：“这是一个问题，这是它的认可答案。”但标记只是给原本已经独立成立的段落做注释。它是路标，不是写作本身的替代品。

### 结构化答案区块的几种形式

这种模式通常表现为几种反复出现的形式：

- **问答对**——明确的问题后紧跟直接回答，FAQ 板块和[其他人还问](https://roborank.io/glossary/people-also-ask/)结果就采用这种形式。
- **定义区块**——术语后立即跟上一个独立完整的定义，本词汇表每页顶部都使用这一形式。
- **直接回答段落**——用两三句直白的话，简要回答“如何”或“为什么”，多数[精选摘要](https://roborank.io/glossary/featured-snippet/)取自这种形式。

无论哪种形式，规则都相同：一个含义完整的单元，能够独立成立，表达方式让机器可以引用它，而无需一并携带周边页面内容。

### 结构化答案区块示例

有关答案区块最清楚的现实经验，恰恰来自 Google 取消一种奖励。**2023 年 8 月**，Google 在 Search Central 博客发布*《[HowTo 和 FAQ 富媒体搜索结果的变化](https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2023/08/howto-faq-changes)》*，宣布 FAQ 富媒体结果——从 FAQPage 结构化数据生成、可以展开的问答摘要——此后只向“知名、权威的政府和医疗健康网站”开放。对其他网站，这种富媒体结果将不再经常显示。同一篇文章也彻底弃用了 HowTo 富媒体结果。

随后，Google 完成了后续调整。FAQ 富媒体结果从搜索中全面退场，从 **2026 年 5 月 7 日**开始推出变化；相关 Search Console 报告和富媒体搜索结果测试支持，也计划在随后数月内移除。Google 的指导很直接：可以保留 FAQPage 标记，但它不会再对搜索中的可见展示产生影响。

这段经历的启发大于打击，原因就在这里。把 FAQ 富媒体结果当作全部目标的团队，只剩下一堆不起作用的标记；而把它用来落实写作要求——每条 FAQ 都写成清楚、自成一体的问答对——的团队，仍然持续获益，因为精选摘要和 AI 答案引擎提取的，恰好也是这些区块。可见的展示位置变了，但底层资产——机器可以完整引用的段落——价值丝毫未减。区块始终才是产品，schema 从来只是贴在上面的标签。

### 人们常犯的错误

人们的错误，是追逐标记，而不是把区块写好。多年来，团队给任何带问号的内容都硬加 FAQPage schema，把富媒体结果当成奖品。后来 Google 取消这一展示，很多工作看起来都白做了。真正重要的从来不是 schema 本身。结构化答案区块之所以有价值，是因为机器能清楚地引用它，无论回报是精选摘要、AI 概览中的一句话，还是 ChatGPT 里的引用，这一点都成立。把答案写得能够独立成立——一个问题、一个直接表达的答案，没有“正如上文讨论过的”——标记就只是给原本适合引用的段落再加一点小帮助。跳过这一步，任何 schema 都救不了它。

### 常见问题

#### 什么是结构化答案区块？

它是一段经过写作和排版设计、能够被整体提取为问题直接答案的文字，可以是问答对、定义或独立成立的简短概述。搜索引擎和 AI 系统偏爱这类区块，因为提取时不需要页面其他内容。

#### 创建答案区块必须使用 FAQ schema 吗？

不需要。FAQPage 结构化数据等标记可以给区块贴标签，但区块单凭文字本身就可以发挥作用。精选摘要和 AI 答案经常引用没有任何结构化数据、但清楚且自成一体的段落。可提取性来自表达方式，而非标签。

#### Google 为什么移除 FAQ 富媒体搜索结果？

2023 年 8 月，作为简化搜索展示的一部分，Google 将 FAQ 富媒体结果范围缩小为权威政府和医疗健康网站；此后全面停用，并从 2026 年 5 月 7 日开始推出调整。底层 FAQPage 标记仍然有效，只是不再产生那种视觉展示结果。

#### 结构化答案区块如今出现在哪里？

它们出现在精选摘要、“其他人还问”，并越来越多地进入 Google AI Overviews、Perplexity 和 ChatGPT 等 AI 答案中。这些系统会提取自成一体的段落作为回答。展示场景变了，可引用区块的价值没有变。

### 结论

结构化答案区块是为提取而组织的内容：一个问题，对应一个表达直接、不依赖上下文、可被机器逐字引用的答案。FAQPage 等 schema 可以为其标注，但力量从不在标签里，而在足够清楚、能够直接提取的段落里。当可见回报从 FAQ 富媒体结果转向精选摘要和 AI 答案时，能够独立成立的区块，仍会不断被选中。

## 英文原文

A structured answer block is a self-contained passage — often a question paired with a short answer, a definition, or a direct summary — written so a search or AI system can extract it whole and present it as the answer to a query. It states one claim plainly, needs no surrounding page for context, and is sometimes reinforced with markup such as FAQPage structured data.

### Key Takeaways

- A structured answer block pairs a clear question or query with a self-contained answer, so an engine can extract it without the rest of the page.
- FAQPage structured data is the [schema.org](http://schema.org) markup most associated with answer blocks, but the block earns AI citations and featured snippets even with no markup at all.
- In August 2023 Google announced FAQ rich results would only show for authoritative government and health sites; it then fully retired FAQ rich results in Search, with the change rolling out from May 7, 2026.
- The durable value of an answer block is extractability — a passage that survives being quoted alone is what AI answers, featured snippets, and People Also Ask select.

### How Structured Answer Blocks Work

A retrieval or answer engine does not quote pages; it quotes passages. When Google builds a featured snippet, or when an AI system writes an [AI Overview](https://roborank.io/glossary/ai-overviews/), it scans candidate documents for a span of text that answers the query on its own and can be presented with little or no editing. A structured answer block is content deliberately shaped to be that span: a question or implied query, immediately met by a short, self-contained answer.

What makes a block “structured” is less about markup than about form. The answer leads — it does not bury the point under preamble — and it carries no dangling references to the rest of the page. This is the discipline of [answer-first writing](https://roborank.io/glossary/answer-first-writing/): put the claim in the first sentence, then support it. A block written this way is [extractable](https://roborank.io/glossary/extractability/), meaning it survives being copied into an answer with zero surrounding context. A block that starts with “As mentioned above, this depends on several factors” cannot be lifted, no matter how correct it is.

Markup can label the block for machines. FAQPage structured data, for instance, tells a parser “this is a question and this is its accepted answer.” But the markup only annotates a passage that already stands on its own — it is a signpost, not a substitute for the writing.

### Forms a Structured Answer Block Takes

The pattern shows up in a few recurring shapes:

- **The Q&A pair** — an explicit question followed by a direct answer, the form behind FAQ sections and [People Also Ask](https://roborank.io/glossary/people-also-ask/) results.
- **The definition block** — a term followed immediately by a self-contained definition, the form this glossary uses at the top of every page.
- **The direct-answer paragraph** — a short summary that resolves a “how” or “why” query in two or three plain sentences, the form most [featured snippets](https://roborank.io/glossary/featured-snippet/) are drawn from.

In every shape the rule is the same: one unit of meaning, complete on its own, phrased so a machine can quote it without inheriting the page around it.

### Example of a Structured Answer Block

The clearest real-world lesson about answer blocks came from Google itself taking a reward away. On its Search Central blog in **August 2023**, in a post titled *[“Changes to HowTo and FAQ rich results”](https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2023/08/howto-faq-changes)*, Google announced that FAQ rich results — the expandable Q&A snippets drawn from FAQPage structured data — would from then on be shown only for “well-known, authoritative government and health websites.” For every other site, the rich result would no longer appear regularly. The same post deprecated HowTo rich results outright.

Google then finished the job. FAQ rich results were retired from Search entirely, with the rollout beginning **May 7, 2026**, and the associated Search Console reports and Rich Results Test support scheduled for removal in the months after. Google’s guidance was blunt: you can leave the FAQPage markup in place, but it will have no visible effect in Search.

Here is why the episode is instructive rather than depressing. The teams that had treated the FAQ rich result as the whole point were left with markup that did nothing. The teams that had used it to enforce a discipline — writing every FAQ as a clean, self-contained question-and-answer pair — kept winning, because those same blocks are exactly what featured snippets and AI answer engines lift. The visible venue changed; the underlying asset, a passage a machine can quote whole, did not lose an ounce of value. The block was always the product, and the schema was only ever the label on it.

### The thing people get wrong

The thing people get wrong is chasing the markup instead of writing the block. For years teams bolted FAQPage schema onto anything with a question mark, treating the rich result as the prize — and then Google took the rich result away and a lot of that work looked wasted. It wasn’t the schema that ever mattered. A structured answer block earns its keep because a machine can quote it cleanly, and that is true whether the reward is a featured snippet, a line in an AI Overview, or a citation in ChatGPT. Write the answer so it stands on its own — one question, one plainly stated answer, no “as we discussed above” — and the markup becomes a small bonus on top of a passage that was already quotable. Skip that and no schema will save it.

### Frequently Asked Questions

#### What is a structured answer block?

It is a passage written and formatted to be extracted whole as a direct answer to a question — a Q&A pair, a definition, or a short summary that stands alone. Search engines and AI systems favor these blocks because they can lift them without the surrounding page.

#### Do I need FAQ schema to create an answer block?

No. Markup like FAQPage structured data can label a block, but the block works on its writing alone. Featured snippets and AI answers routinely quote clean, self-contained passages that carry no structured data — extractability comes from the phrasing, not the tags.

#### Why did Google remove FAQ rich results?

Google narrowed FAQ rich results to authoritative government and health sites in August 2023 as part of a broader simplification of search appearances, then retired them entirely, rolling the change out from May 7, 2026. The underlying FAQPage markup is still valid; it just no longer produces that visual result.

#### Where do structured answer blocks show up now?

In featured snippets, People Also Ask, and — increasingly — inside AI answers from Google AI Overviews, Perplexity, and ChatGPT, which lift a self-contained passage as the response. The venue changed; the value of a quotable block did not.

### The Bottom Line

A structured answer block is content packaged for extraction: one question met by one plainly stated, context-free answer that a machine can quote verbatim. Schema like FAQPage can annotate it, but the power was never in the tags — it is in a passage clean enough to lift. As the visible reward shifts from FAQ rich results to featured snippets and AI answers, the block that stands on its own is the one that keeps getting picked.
